sentences.text:
For Respondent(s) : Mr. J.P. Bhardwaj, Pp.
_____________________________________________________ Hon'Ble The
Chief Justice Judgment 06/07/2017
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. Case of the prosecution is that Kunj Bihari Bhardwaj (PW-1), the Food Inspector, in presence of Kanak Mal Jain (PW-2), a shop owner and Mohan Singh (PW-3), an employee of the department purchased 'Khoya' (Mawa) from the petitioner.
Sent to the public analyst for analysis, vide report Exhibit P-7 dated 19 th December, 1986, the sample was found to be adulterated inasmuch as milk fat content detected was 18%.

As per the prescribed standard it had to be 20%.
3.
The defence taken by the petitioner is that he was not in the business of sale of 'Khoya'.
He had purchased the same for domestic consumption.

4. I find that the three witnesses of the prosecution who have deposed that Inspector Kunj Bihari Bhardwaj purchased the (2 of 3) [CRLR-518/1996] 'Khoya' from the petitioner were given suggestions to this effect.
Even in the statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. the petitioner has said so.

5. Whilst it may be true that this aspect would relate to an appreciation of evidence and the finding returned by the learned Magistrate is that there is credible evidence to prove that the petitioner sold sample to the Inspector, but a critical feature of the circumstance impacting of the evidence have been overlooked.
The circumstance is that as per the prosecution the sample was taken when the petitioner was standing at the bus stand.
Meaning thereby, the petitioner was not carrying on business from a shop.
6. That apart, there is a serious infirmity in the prosecution evidence which has been glossed over by the learned Magistrate as also the learned Court of the Sessions which heard the appeal.

7. It is settled law that a notice under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 Bapu Lal vs State on 6 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164775675/
1 is a mandatory notice to be given and proved to have been given.
'Given' means 'served' upon the accused.
The reason is a valuable right created in favour of the accused to request for a second sample to be sent to the Central Food Laboratory.
8. In the instant case, a carbon copy of the purported notice allegedly sent to the petitioner was filed along with the complaint but has not been proved.
The same is a carbon copy of the notice drawn up to be served upon the petitioner.
There are no signature of the petitioner thereon evincing service thereof upon the petitioner.
No postal receipt has been produced to evidence dispatch by post.
No A.D. card has been proved.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Conviction of the petitioner and sentence to undergo six months R.I. and to pay fine in sum of 1,000/- in the decision dated 18 th November, 1991 passed by the learned Magistrate is set aside.

The petitioner is acquitted of the charge for having committed offence punishable under Section 6 read with Section 17 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954.
10.
The bail bonds and surety bonds furnished by the petitioner on being granted by this Court are discharged.

(PRADEEP NANDRAJOG)CJ.
